request.name: Govinda
request.title: Actor
request.about:
Govinda Arun Ahuja (born 21 December 1963), known mononymously as Govinda is an Indian actor-turned-politician, who has appeared in more than 165 Hindi-language films. A leading actor throughout 1990s, he is known for his slapstick performances and dancing skills. He has received 12 Filmfare Award nominations and won two Filmfare Special Awards and one Filmfare Award for Best Comedian.

Starting out as an action and dancing hero in the 1980s, his first film was 1986's Love 86, which turned out to be a hit. He then appeared in subsequent hits including Ilzaam (1986), Marte Dam Tak (1987), Khudgarz (1987), Dariya Dil (1988), Jaisi Karni Waisi Bharni (1989), Swarg (1990) and Hum (1991). However, Govinda would go on to reinvent himself as a comic hero in the 1990s after his role as a mischievous young NCC cadet in the 1992 romance Shola Aur Shabnam and 1993 action comedy Aankhen in which he played dual role. Following the success of these films, Govinda had lead roles in several commercially successful comedy films, like Raja Babu (1994), Coolie No. 1 (1995), Saajan Chale Sasural (1996), Hero No. 1 (1997), Deewana Mastana (1997), Dulhe Raja (1998), Bade Miyan Chote Miyan (1998), Anari No.1 (1999), Haseena Maan Jayegi (1999) and Jodi No. 1 (2001). He won the Filmfare Special Award for Saajan Chale Sasural and the Filmfare Award for Best Comedian for Haseena Maan Jaayegi.

After a series of several unsuccessful films in the 2000s, his later commercial hits include Bhagam Bhag (2006), Partner (2007), and Holiday (2014). In 2015, Govinda became a judge on Zee TV's reality show, Dance India Dance Super Moms.

Govinda was a member of the Parliament of India from 2004 to 2009. As the Indian National Congress party member, he was elected as Member of Parliament (MP) form the Mumbai North constituency of Maharashtra, India in the Lok Sabha elections of 2004. In 2024, just before the Lok Sabha elections, he joined Shivsena.

events.event: Officially announced his major cinematic comeback as a lead actor and producer with the upcoming film 'Roopa', addressing past career declines and years of being written off by the industry.

Faced widespread media speculation and public controversy regarding his marriage after reports surfaced claiming he and his wife Sunita Ahuja were heading for a divorce, accompanied by public allegations of infidelity.
Experienced a health scare and was rushed to CritiCare Asia Multispeciality Hospital in Mumbai after falling unconscious.
Suffered a serious leg injury and underwent surgery after his licensed revolver accidentally went off at his Mumbai residence, sparking intense media attention and public concern.

Faced legal repercussions and was directed by the Supreme Court of India to issue an apology and pay compensation following a long-standing 2008 assault controversy where he slapped a struggling actor on a film set.
Elected as a Member of Parliament in the 14th Lok Sabha representing the Mumbai North constituency under the Indian National Congress (resigned in 2009).
Welcomed the birth of his son, Yashvardhan Ahuja, with his wife Sunita Ahuja.
Welcomed the birth of his daughter, Tina Ahuja, with his wife Sunita Ahuja.
Married his wife Sunita Ahuja in a private ceremony.
Made his Bollywood acting debut as a leading man in the action film 'Love 86', directed by E. V. V. Satyanarayana and produced by Pahlaj Nihalani.
Born as Govind Arun Ahuja in Mumbai, Maharashtra, India, to actor-producer Arun Kumar Ahuja and classical singer-actress Nirmala Devi.
